limitations: The reviewer is a separate Claude agent session on the same host and the same account as the producer. The producer session launched it. It is not a second machine and not a human. The same reviewer session rejected the v6 build and then reviewed this rebuilt v7 build.

Capture provenance is archived and was not re-acquired. The reviewer did not run Pi. Root completeness, the Pi build 1.0.0, the model, the provider and the operating system rest on retained capture receipts. The native session file does not record the Pi build.

The replay ran the packet's own copy of the scoring code under macOS sandbox-exec on the producer's host with Python 3.14.7. It shows determinism and integrity. It is not an independent implementation of the scorer.

The observer for turns, responses, actions and results is the stdout event stream of the same Pi process. Its 13 message_end objects equal the 13 native message records. It is independent of the session file, not of the harness. Only the helper ledger and the workspace file hashes are independent of the harness.

The changed-file fact depends on the workload: the inspect helper prints the whole pre-edit file and its digest into a tool result. The scorer still takes the workspace path string from the capture plan to make the edit target relative; that string equals the cwd in the native session header in all three runs.

attribution.token_semantics is scored on four explicit integer fields. The scorer does not test the estimated or billed distinction named in the rubric row. The same rule applies to every configuration.

attribution.reconciliation is native_absent under the rubric text amended on 2026-10-03, after the earlier v5 result was known. The reviewer agrees with the state: the file declares no session or turn total, although its six per-message usage records sum exactly to the Pi RPC total. The reviewer did not use git and cannot confirm that the amended rubric is committed.

portable.isolated_decode and portable.canonical_equality are set true by construction in the replay code. The sandboxed replay shows that the decode works from packet bytes alone and that the diagnostics digest equals the build-time digest.

The reviewer cannot read the plaintext of the encrypted reasoning blobs. The packets also publish provider response and call ids, device:inode values, /private/tmp scratch paths and per-request cost values. None identifies a person as far as the reviewer can determine.

Hash test for a guessed home user name: 118 distinct SHA-256 values per packet. 116 resolve to bytes inside the packet. expected_diagnostics_sha256 resolves to the replay diagnostics, which hold no home path. model_catalog_sha256 is the digest of the Pi model list output, whose pre-image is not in the packet; the reviewer could not recompute it without running Pi. No tested user-name or home-path string matches any published digest.

Published files still label themselves public_safe false, scope private_native_to_score_diagnostics and score_eligible false, because the validator requires these constants. inputs/pi-format holds MIT-licensed vendor documents without the license text.
The reviewer did not re-review the Claude CLI packets. It only read that the amended File change rule and the shared inspect_checkout_source helper exist.
